description: This figure is a single rectangular table rendered as an image, presented on a white background with black text and horizontal rules; there are no micrographs, curves or photographs. The bold header reads "Table 7 – EDS for Al and Mn in 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C." The leftmost column is headed "wt%" and the table is split into two element blocks, "Al" and "Mn", each subdivided into three phase columns labelled "δ", "γ" and "k" (delta-ferrite, austenite and kappa-carbide). The three data rows are labelled "Min", "Mean" and "max" (printed with that lower-case spelling). Reading across: Al Min = 11.0, 5.7, 10.3 for δ, γ, k; Al Mean = 11.9, 7.8, 10.8; Al max = 13.6, 9.9, 11.9; Mn Min = 15.2, 20.3, 21.9; Mn Mean = 17.9, 23.6, 23.9; Mn max = 20.8, 27.6, 25.5. All values are in wt%. The table therefore reports EDS-measured Al and Mn partitioning between the three phases, showing Al is highest in δ-ferrite and lowest in γ, while Mn is lowest in δ and highest in γ and k. No scale bars, axes or legends are present; nothing in the image is illegible.

observations.observation: The figure is a text table titled 'Table 7 – EDS for Al and Mn in 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C.'
The table reports Al and Mn contents in wt% for three phases labelled δ, γ and k.
Table rows are labelled Min, Mean and max.
Within every row Al is highest in δ and lowest in γ, indicating Al partitions to δ-ferrite and is depleted in austenite.
Within every row Mn is lowest in δ and highest in γ (and comparable/higher in k), indicating Mn partitions to austenite and k phase and is depleted in δ-ferrite.
The mean Al content of the γ phase (7.8 wt%) is below the nominal 12 wt% Al, while the mean Al of δ (11.9 wt%) and k (10.8 wt%) is near nominal.
The measured data pertain to the alloy 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C.
